newsitem.title: UK: Late bond market prices - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: Late bond market prices - Feb 27.

text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.

GERMANY - Bund futures rebounded convincingly from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks, pushing the spread against Treasuries further into record territory. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.62, up 0.55 from Wednesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts picked themselves up again after their battering from Greenspan and strode higher, helped by firmer Bunds and T-bonds. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-07/32, up 18/32 from Wednesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bonds shrugged off strong U.S. economic data to climb to their highest level for a week but traders said the gains were fragile and there was a limit to how long European bonds could outperform the United States. The March bond future on the MATIF exchange in Paris settled at 132.40, up 0.4 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets looked pale and weak as concerns over the prospects for European economic and monetary union continued to buffet them in choppy trade. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.83, down 0.40 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened weaker and posted modest losses following strong durable goods orders in January. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-03/32, up 07/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.79 percent.

JAPAN - The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended easier, pushed down by position-adjustment sales that appeared towards the close. In after-hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.28, down 0.02 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Eurobond volumes were fairly low as bond markets recovered from Wednesday's falls following comments from Alan Greenspan. The New Zealand dollar sector saw two new issues, a three-year deal from the World Bank and a four-year bond from Dresdner Bank. Toronto-Dominion Bank launched a $200 million subordinated fixed/FRN transaction. ING and GECC issued short-dated dollar bonds.
